Aisha (CSM): Quick dry-run of the SLA credits playbook for Maple Health onboarding — can we run through 3 common scenarios and confirm the external messaging?
Priya (Ops): Yes. I can simulate uptime and p50/p95 latency deltas. When do you want to do the walk-through? :calendar: 
Tom (Support): I can bring the customer-facing email drafts and the one-pager on credit calculations.
Aisha (CSM): Thanks. Goal is to validate wording + numbers so renewals team has a script. Also need to flag any onboarding gaps that increase renewal risk.
Ben (Product): Quick note: recent runtime change reduced tail latency variance, so our p99 exposures are lower than last quarter. Should affect credit thresholds.
Priya (Ops): I ran two dry queries against the simulation harness: 
```
Scenario A: transient pod OOM during config push -> 4m outage -> recorded uptime 99.994% over window -> credit = 10% per current table
Scenario B: sustained latency increase due to cache warmup -> p95 from 420ms -> 950ms for ~12m -> credits triggered by latency SLO breach rule B2
```
Aisha (CSM): Nice. Tom, can you try an email draft that explains scenario B without sounding too alarmist? Keep it: cause, impact, mitigation, credit.
Tom (Support): Draft v1: 
"We observed a temporary increase in request latency during your onboarding due to cache warmup after model import. Impacted calls saw p95 ~950ms for 12 minutes. We\u2019ve applied a 5% service credit per the SLA and pushed a config to reduce future warmups."
Aisha (CSM): Love the structure. Suggest replace "we\u2019ve applied" with "we will apply" until finance confirms. Also include a one-line action for the customer (restart import if they want to accelerate warm cache).
Ben (Product): Also add that Dedicated customers can pin quantized variants to avoid warmups — one-liner.
eng-deploy-bot: deployment maple-onboard-config v2 -> success (3141592701) :white_check_mark:
Priya (Ops): Small policy ask: should we cap credits for onboarding windows? Currently table allows multiple credits stackable which could be big for multi-step imports.
Aisha (CSM): Good call. For onboarding phase we usually cap to one credit per incident type per 24h. That needs to be explicit in the external doc.
Tom (Support): I'll create an external note with cap language and link to the credit calculator. 
Tom (Support): link: https://redwood.example/sla/credits-calc?customer=maple
Priya (Ops): One more simulation: what if there is a routing fallback to region B? Customer sees increased latency but no outage. Rule currently treats that as latency-only credit. Confirm?
Ben (Product): Correct — fallback -> no uptime breach -> latency SLO evaluation only. But we should include an example of routing fallback in the playbook so CS reps can explain it clearly.
Aisha (CSM): Action items: 
- Tom: publish external note + email draft v2 with finance-safe phrasing (due EOD)
- Priya: run one more sim with multi-import overlap and share numbers (due tomorrow)
- Ben: add one-liner about dedicated pinning and routing fallback to playbook (due EOD)
- Me (Aisha): update renewal risk flagging doc with potential credit exposure thresholds
Priya (Ops): Acked. I'll attach the sim logs when done.
Tom (Support): Will push draft to Google Drive and ping legal for the phrasing check.
Ben (Product): Ping me if you want a short blurb for the product appendix.
Aisha (CSM): Thanks all. If anyone hears from Maple execs before we finish, @Aisha will handle direct comms. :thumbsup:
eng-deploy-bot: heartbeat - infra metrics snapshot attached (3141592785)
Aisha (CSM): wrapping up here — last message before I consolidate into the playbook. Good dry-run, helped surface the onboarding cap policy.
